chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:

The Muhrim (person in Ihram), if he kills game, upon him is its compensation, and he gives the game as charity to a poor person.' This does not contradict what we mentioned, because his saying (peace be upon him): 'and he gives the game as charity to a poor person' implies that he meant if it still has vitality, requiring slaughter in that state, so the Muahl (one out of Ihram) slaughters it and eats it if it is in Ihram, and similarly is the report which was narrated.

key_terms.الْحِلُّ: The state of being out of Ihram
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a pilgrim in Ihram who kills game, and how is the meat handled?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi reconciles this narration with previous discussions by interpreting the command to give the game as charity as conditional upon the prey retaining vitality (ramaq), which requires the pilgrim to slaughter it upon exiting Ihram. This specific mechanism ensures that the compensation is physically realized through the animal itself, distinguishing it from monetary or other forms of fidya. The ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical state of the prey determining the method of expiation.
